```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(gganimate)
library(ggridges)
library(dygraphs)
library(janitor)

# Dataset from https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aniruddhasshirahatti/us-unemployment-dataset-2010-2020?resource=download

unemp_data <- read_csv(
  "C:\\Users\\Avery Shaw\\Downloads\\unemployment_data_us.csv",
  col_names = FALSE,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

unemp_data <- unemp_data |>  
  row_to_names(row_number = 1) |>
  mutate(
    Date = as.Date(paste(Year, Month, "01"), format = "%Y %b %d"),
    Primary_School= parse_number(Primary_School),
    High_School = parse_number(High_School),
    Associates_Degree = parse_number(Associates_Degree),
    Professional_Degree = parse_number(Professional_Degree),
    White = parse_number(White),
    Black = parse_number(Black),
    Asian = parse_number(Asian),
    Hispanic = parse_number(Hispanic),
    Men = parse_number(Men),
    Women = parse_number(Women)
  ) |> 
  select(-Year, -Month)

unemp_data <- unemp_data |>
  relocate(Date, .before = 1)

```


## {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="margin-top: 100px;"}
What is dygraphs?

::: {.incremental .fade-up}
- A package for R that provides an interface to the dygraphs JavaScript charting library
- It is built for creating highly interactive, fast-rendering time-series charts
- Can only be included in HTML based R Markdown formats
- Uses a date/time variable as the time index (x-axis), which should be stored in a recognized format, such as R's built-in `Date` class.
:::
:::

::: footer
Learn more: [dygraphs](https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/articles/dygraphs.html)
:::

## Data Set - U.S. Unemployment 2010-2020

```{r}
unemp_data |> 
  slice_head(n=6)
```

## `dygraph()` arguments

``` {.r code-line-numbers="2|3-5|6|7-8"}
library(dygraph)
dygraph(unemp_data,
    main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends Across Demographic and Educational Groups (2010–2020)",
    xlab = "Year",
    ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    group = NULL,
    width = 1000,
    height = 600)
```

## Plot with `dygraph` arguments

```{r}
dygraph(unemp_data,
  main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends Across Demographic and Educational Groups (2010–2020)",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
  group = "unemployment",
  width = 1000,
  height = 600)
```

::: footer
Learn more: [dygraphs](https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/articles/dygraphs.html)
:::



## `dyRangeSelector()` {auto-animate="true"}

-   Adds a range selector below the graph that lets users zoom in on a specific date range.

. . .

``` {.r code-line-numbers="5|6|7|8-9|10-11"}
dygraph(unemp_data,
        width = 1000,
        height = 600) 
        |> 
  dyRangeSelector(
  dateWindow = c("2010-01-01", "2015-01-01"),
  height = 40,
  fillColor = "lightgreen",
  strokeColor = "navy",
  keepMouseZoom = TRUE,
  retainDateWindow = FALSE
  )
```

::: footer
Learn more: [dyRangeSelector](https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/reference/dyRangeSelector.html?q=dyran#null)
:::

## Plot with Range Selector

```{r}
dygraph(unemp_data,
        main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends Across Demographic and Educational Groups (2010–2020)",
        xlab = "Year",
        ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
        width = 1000,
        height = 600) |> 
  dyRangeSelector(
  dateWindow = c("2010-01-01", "2015-01-01"),
  height = 40,
  fillColor = "lightgreen",
  strokeColor = "navy",
  keepMouseZoom = TRUE,
  retainDateWindow = FALSE
  )
```

::: footer
Learn more: [dyRangeSelector](https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/reference/dyRangeSelector.html?q=dyran#null)
:::

## `dySeries()` {auto-animate="true"}

- Changes the appearance of a line on the dygraph

. . .

``` {.r code-line-numbers="4|5|6|7-9|10-11|13-16"}
unemp_data |>
  select(Date, Men, Women) |>
  dygraph()|>
  dySeries("Men",
           label = "Men",
           color = "blue",
           stepPlot = FALSE,
           stemPlot = FALSE,
           fillGraph = FALSE,
           strokeWidth = 3,
           strokePattern = "dashed"
           )|>
  dySeries("Women", 
            label = "Women",
            color = "red",
            strokeWidth = 2) |> 
  dyRangeSelector()
  
```

::: footer
Learn more: [dySeries](https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/reference/dySeries.html?q=dyser#null)
:::

## Plot with `dySeries`

```{r}
unemp_data |>
```

## `dyOptions()` {auto-animate="true"}

- Controls the overall appearance and behavior of the graph through various display options.

. . .

``` {.r code-line-numbers="7|8-11|12-14|15-17|18-19|20-25|26"}
unemp_data |>
  select(Date, Primary_School, High_School, Associates_Degree, Professional_Degree) |>
  dygraph(main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends by Educational Level (2010–2020)",
          xlab = "Date",
          ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)"
          )|>
dyOptions(
  stackedGraph = FALSE,
  fillGraph = FALSE,
  stepPlot = FALSE,
  stemPlot = FALSE,
  drawPoints = FALSE,
  pointSize = 2,
  pointShape = ("square"),
  strokeWidth = 2,
  strokeBorderColor = NULL,
  colors = c("violet", "orange", "royalblue", "forestgreen"),
  drawXAxis = TRUE,
  drawYAxis = TRUE,
  axisTickSize = 3,
  axisLineColor = "red",
  axisLineWidth = 0.3,
  axisLabelColor = "red",
  axisLabelFontSize = 14,
  axisLabelWidth = 80,
  drawGrid = TRUE
) 
```

## Plot with `dyOptions()` {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
unemp_data |>
  select(Date, Primary_School, High_School, Associates_Degree, Professional_Degree) |>
  dygraph(main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends by Educational Level (2010–2020)",
          xlab = "Date",
          ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)"
          )|>
dyOptions(
  stackedGraph = FALSE,
  fillGraph = FALSE,
  stepPlot = FALSE,
  stemPlot = FALSE,
  drawPoints = FALSE,
  pointSize = 2,
  pointShape = ("square"),
  strokeWidth = 2,
  strokeBorderColor = NULL,
  colors = c("violet", "orange", "royalblue", "forestgreen"),
  drawXAxis = TRUE,
  drawYAxis = TRUE,
  axisTickSize = 3,
  axisLineColor = "red",
  axisLineWidth = 0.3,
  axisLabelColor = "red",
  axisLabelFontSize = 14,
  axisLabelWidth = 80,
  drawGrid = TRUE
) 
```


## "group" argument in `dygraph` {auto-animate="true"}

- Allows multiple graphs to be linked together so their date-range selections and zooming stay synchronized.

. . .

``` {.r code-line-numbers="1,7|2,8|3,9|4-5,10"}
unemp_data |> 
    select(Date, Men, Women) |> 
    dygraph(group = "unemployment") |>
    dyOptions(colors = c("blue", "red")) |> 
  dyRangeSelector()
  
  unemp_data |> 
    select(Date, Black, White, Hispanic, Asian) |> 
    dygraph(group = "unemployment") |>
  dyRangeSelector()
```


## Comparing Plots (with group argument from `dygraph`)

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
unemp_data |> 
    select(Date, Men, Women) |> 
    dygraph(group = "unemployment",
            main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends by Gender (2010–2020)",
          xlab = "Date",
          ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)") |>
    dyOptions(colors = c("blue", "red")) |> 
  dyRangeSelector()
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
unemp_data |> 
    select(Date, Black, White, Hispanic, Asian) |> 
    dygraph(group = "unemployment",
            main = "U.S. Unemployment Trends by Race & Ethnicity (2010–2020)",
          xlab = "Date",
          ylab = "Unemployment Rate (%)") |>
  dyRangeSelector()
```
:::

:::


## Summary

::: {.incremental .fade-left}
- `dygraph()` – Creates an interactive time-series graph.
- `dyRangeSelector()` – Adds a tool to zoom in on date ranges.
- `dySeries()` – Customizes individual data lines.
- `dyOptions()` – Customizes overall graph appearance and behavior.
:::

::: footer
Learn more: [dygraphs](https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/articles/dygraphs.html)
:::
